STEP 1 - Scene: A plate of roasted Brussels sprouts, photographed from directly above (top-down view).

STEP 2 - Ruler: A square/rounded white plate, roughly 26 cm across at its widest. Area ≈ 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2. (Shape is squarish, so area is approximate.)

STEP 3 - Items: About 11 whole roasted Brussels sprouts, some charred/browned on the outer leaves. No visible sauce or oil pool.

STEP 4 - Area: The sprouts are clustered in the center-left of the plate and a few sit on the right. Together they cover roughly 25% of the plate area (about 130 cm^2). Roasted Brussels sprouts: ~25%.

STEP 5 - Volume: Each sprout is about 3 to 3.5 cm in diameter and about 3 cm tall; they are piled in a loose layer, so the outer envelope is about 2.5 cm high on average. Volume ≈ 130 cm^2 x 2.5 cm ≈ 325 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole sprouts are dense-ish but have gaps between them. Bulk density for cut/whole vegetables ~0.5-0.6 g/ml. Using 0.55: 325 x 0.55 ≈ 179 g. Sanity check: 11 sprouts at roughly 15-20 g each (cooked) gives about 165-220 g, consistent.

STEP 7 - Energy: Roasted Brussels sprouts, cooked, ~35-45 kcal per 100 g (they may have a little oil from roasting, which pushes it up). Use 40 kcal/100 g. 179 g x 40 kcal/100 g ≈ 72 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: Eleven small roasted sprouts, about 180 g, around 70 kcal is plausible. Hidden oil from roasting could add some energy, but none is visible, so I've not added any.

Total: about 180 g, about 70 kcal.
